title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID as a member of the Polo caravan: Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar died in 1099, some 170 years before the journey, and was Castilian, not Venetian
FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA in the caravan: the Hohenstaufen emperor drowned in 1190 and never travelled the Silk Road; presumably stands in for Niccolo Polo, who is named in the text but never placed

Knights and Crossbowmen as caravan escort: the Polos travelled as a tiny merchant party with local guides and Mongol paiza-holders, not a Latin heavy-cavalry retinue; Trade Carts, camels or light foot would have been available in the engine
SHEEP used as the caravan's 'pack animals' when camels (Camel Rider / domesticated camel objects) and Trade Carts exist in the catalogue and are the iconic Silk Road transport

Shangdu represented by a plain European TOWN_CENTER plus two Gaia yurts; the Khan's summer palace could have been suggested with East Asian-style buildings, a Wonder, or Mongol/Chinese architecture set pieces
Kublai Khan himself is entirely absent from the objects despite the victory text describing Marco standing before him
